findings.title: Event-granted Aedui Battle accepts Ambush in multiple Regions
findings.expected: Aedui may Ambush in only one Region per Battle Command, including Assembly of Gaul’s free Command; both ordinary and Event interfaces must reject a two-Region Ambush before it executes.
findings.observed: Card 52 shaded accepts a human single-SA plan with Ambush in Carnutes and Mandubii. Each Region begins with six Hidden Aedui and five Revealed Belgae. Both finish at six Aedui/two Belgae, avoiding the second Region’s otherwise required one-Warband Counterattack loss. The one-Ambush control finishes Mandubii at five Aedui/two Belgae. The ordinary Command+SA validator and Assembly’s two-ability schema both reject the same excessive Ambush scope.
findings.cause: free_actions._plan_structure_error checks Aedui Ambush scope only for Morasses; its generic free Command+SA route omits the normal action validator’s one-Region guard. _execute_battle validates each Ambush locally without enforcing the Command-wide cap.

source_refs.quote: the Aedui may only Ambush in a maximum of one Region per Battle Command.
Faction Controlling Carnutes Region executes a Command that may add 2 Special Abilities, free.
The shaded actions are all free but have to follow the usual rules for space selection and so forth

source_refs.description: 3.1.2 retains other requirements/procedures for free actions unless Event text modifies them.

findings.fixture: Controlled Great Revolt seed4 second-edition position using build_initial_state and place_piece; permanent Provincia Fort retained, six Aedui versus five Revealed Belgae in each of two Regions, Aedui Control Carnutes. Pre/post census and structural integrity clean. No NPC decisions or stochastic hard-piece saves needed. Defenders explicitly choose to stand in legal normal-Battle control.
findings.controls: Same two-Region plan is rejected unchanged under an ordinary Command+SA. Assembly two-ability schema also rejects it. One-Ambush free Battle succeeds and incurs the expected second-Battle Counterattack loss. Durable SeatSession pauses before the grant, accepts the illegal response after save/load, and replays identically with board/RNG equality. Preview leaves live state/RNG untouched.
findings.prior_relation: FE4-03 exposed only one of Assembly’s two allowed abilities and was fixed by the new multi-ability schema. FE5-01 covered Britannia crossing with an accompanying SA. This is a separate Aedui-specific Command-wide Battle cap in the still-supported single-ability Event response.
findings.limits: Confirmed for numeric52 shaded single-ability human response. No claimed encounter frequency; no claim that NPC Aedui choose this illegal plan.
findings.comparator_pattern: Liberty or Death docs/human_mode_audit.md and lod_ai/event_choices.py: compare rule-defined legal choices and handler validation across frontend/grant paths, not just presence of existing hooks.
findings.repair_recommendation: Share the Aedui one-Ambush-Region constraint across ordinary and free-action validation, preserving the already-correct Assembly multi-ability and Morasses handling; test raw validation, Event execution, and durable sessions.

findings.title: Ariovistus Enlist March cannot divide four Warbands into multiple destination groups
findings.expected: Ariovistus Enlist’s one free German Limited March may select one origin and split its total of at most four affected Warbands into different groups bound for different adjacent Regions, following A3.4.2 and §3.3.2.
findings.observed: The production Enlist collector asks for exactly one origin and destination, then one total/visibility allocation, and returns. execute_free_enlist invokes march_group exactly once with all selected Warbands. Four Germans in Sugambri can be sent entirely to Nervii or partly left behind, but cannot be divided two to Nervii and two to Treveri in the free Command. On the identical Ariovistus board, a public ordinary German Limited Command supports and executes that exact 2+2 split with clean integrity.
findings.cause: enlist_free.py unconditionally retains the base-game one-moving-group schema and implementation for Ariovistus. Its CLI likewise has no group/destination list or continuation. The base single-group rule is replaced by A3.4.2 in the expansion.

source_refs.quote: The German Leader and Warbands March in the same way as Gallic Leaders and Warbands do (3.3.2; not into a 2 nd Region—an effect particular to Vercingetorix).
Pieces within a Region may make up multiple groups.
If this is a Limited Command (2.3.5), select just one origin Region.
execute one free Limited Command with Germanic pieces (per 3.4, making choices as if a Germanic player; no March upon Frost, 2.3.8)

source_refs.description: A4.5.1 changes Enlist, caps four affected German Warbands/Allies and excludes Leader/Settlements and Ariovistus’s Region; it supplies no single-group restriction.
Base §3.4.2 expressly limits German March to one moving group; base one-group behavior remains correct.

findings.fixture: Controlled Ariovistus seed7 position built with piece helpers: permanent Provincia Fort, Belgic Boduognatus/one Belgic Warband at Sugambri, four Hidden Germans there; no German Leader/Settlement present and both destinations empty. Full public Belgic Raid+Enlist executes the terminal-collected single-destination plan. Comparison ordinary German Limited March uses one origin and exactly four Warbands. Pre/post census/structure clean.
findings.controls: Base Great Revolt version uses Ambiorix and correctly permits one group only under §3.4.2. Ariovistus public German Limited March moves two each to Nervii/Treveri. Production terminal collection returns after one destination/total. Both actual Enlist cases execute cleanly and send all selected Germans to the single destination.
findings.prior_relation: Original human-choice inventory SA-ENLIST-FREE verified Rally/Raid and explicitly delegated March/Battle internals. Earlier ledgers address borrowed-force identities and Event-granted transit drop-offs, not Ariovistus’s multiple groups within the free Enlist subcommand. No matching open/closed issue found in rounds1–5.
findings.limits: This is a legal-choice omission demonstrated by the production menu/consumed schema and a source-backed same-board legal split control, not a claim that arbitrary unsupported input must be accepted. It applies only to Ariovistus; base single-group behavior is correct. No frequency estimate or durable replay defect claimed.
findings.comparator_pattern: Liberty or Death docs/human_mode_audit.md opening correction: inventories of existing hooks cannot establish completeness when the choice has no hook; validate against supplied rules.
findings.repair_recommendation: Add Ariovistus group destinations and exact physical allocations to the Enlist free March schema/CLI while enforcing one selected origin, aggregate four-piece cap, once-only movement and existing base single-group rule.

findings.title: Belgic and Arverni offensive Battle forecasts still use pre-Attack defenders and miss Ambiorix strength
findings.expected: Six Belgic Warbands versus six Roman Auxilia should Battle (3 Attack Losses and 1 Counterattack Loss); ten Arverni Warbands versus ten Auxilia should Battle (5 Attack Losses and 2 Counterattack Losses). Ambiorix with two Warbands versus six Auxilia should Battle (3 Attack Losses and 1 Counterattack Loss), whereas a Successor with two Warbands produces 2 Losses on each side and should March. All cases are Command only, with Revealed troops and no relevant Capability or Special Ability.
findings.observed: Public dispatch instead selects and executes March in the favorable equal-starting-troop cases, in both base and Ariovistus for Belgae, and with named Ambiorix. Validated public Battle from the same original states executes with the source-derived losses and clean piece counts.
findings.cause: Each _can_battle_in_region separately estimates Counterattack from the entire initial defender stack. Belgae also value every Warband at one-half even with Ambiorix attacking. Their duplicate _estimate_battle_losses repeats the same arithmetic. Neither consumer uses the corrected surviving-defender forecast already used by Germans.

Counterattack: surviving Defenders cause Losses to Attackers.

findings.controls: Six Belgic Warbands versus four Auxilia and ten Arverni Warbands versus six Auxilia correctly Battle. findings.title: Arverni and Aedui high-value Battle triggers mistake target presence for a forced Loss
findings.expected: Ten Arverni Warbands versus twenty Roman Auxilia and one Legion must March: 5 Attack Losses remove only Auxilia, 8 Counterattack Losses exceed the 5 inflicted, and no Legion absorbs a Loss. Four Aedui Warbands versus a Roman Ally and Fort must not trigger a high-value Battle: the single Attack Loss can be assigned to the Fort while the Ally survives. Forts are absent from the high-value target list in section 8.6.2.
findings.observed: Arverni publicly selects and executes Battle, losing eight Warbands while the Legion remains untouched. Independently, Aedui selects a high_value Battle and the human Roman defender assigns its only Loss to the Fort; the Ally survives. Both execute cleanly and satisfy census checks.
findings.cause: The Arverni can_hit_legion predicate is true whenever any Legion exists and Attack Losses exceed zero, regardless of intervening Auxilia. The Aedui predicate checks high-value target presence and compares losses only with Warbands plus Auxilia, omitting the Fort as a legal alternative loss target.

source_refs.description: Arverni must force at least one Loss (roll or removal) on a Legion, or inflict more than suffered.
Aedui Battle only when sure to inflict Loss on Leader, Ally, Citadel or Legion, accounting for actual defender.
Non-player own-piece losses use reverse removal priority, therefore Auxilia before Legions.
Eligible Forts can absorb Loss by saving roll.
No-Retreat static pieces absorb only after other pieces; Fort and Ally can both remain legal when no mobile defender.

code_refs.description: Any can_hit_legion overrides unfavorable comparative Losses.
The expendable count includes only Warbands plus Auxilia, excluding Forts.

findings.controls: Arverni correctly Marches in the control with the same twenty Auxilia and no Legion (see the NP6-01 table), and correctly Battles the unshielded Legion control. The reviewer's Aedui control without a Fort removes the Ally. The Aedui fixture has two Allies versus one Roman Ally, meeting the victory condition for targeting Romans, and no enemy mobile pieces to introduce Retreat ambiguity.
findings.prior_relation: NP5-02 corrected an Aedui trigger when no high-value piece existed at all; these positions contain real high-value pieces but a Loss is not guaranteed to reach them. NP5-01/NP5-03 concern Diviciacus safety and German comparative forecasts, not forced target identity. Arverni screened-Legion and Aedui Fort-protected Ally share this trigger-guarantee repair group.
findings.comparator_pattern: coin-implementation-lessons.md E: preserve the exact flowchart condition; D: evaluate the specified object, not merely a containing stack.

additional_evidence.fixture: Seed 1; human Romans; four Aedui Warbands against a Roman Ally and Fort; two Aedui Allies elsewhere; permanent Provincia Fort retained. The human callback explicitly assigns the Loss to the Fort.

findings.title: Roman threat gate caps Rampage at two victims and treats impossible Rampages as threats
findings.expected: With three Hidden Belgic Warbands, adjacent Ambiorix, and three Roman Legions plus two Auxilia, a legal Rampage can force a Legion casualty, so R1 should take the Battle/March branch. With two Hidden Belgic Warbands versus three Legions and one Auxilia, Rampage cannot trigger R1 when the Belgic Leader is absent or the Romans have a Fort.
findings.observed: The legal Rampage affecting three victims is ignored, and Romans select and execute Recruit. In both illegal-Rampage variants, Romans select and execute Battle. The matched control with two Hidden Warbands versus two Auxilia correctly does not trigger. The unfortified control with nearby Ambiorix and two Hidden Warbands versus one Auxilia does trigger. Actual Rampage execution from the legal fixtures removes a Legion exactly when required.
findings.cause: roman_bot._has_roman_threat uses min(2, belgic_hidden) without checking Leader range or the exclusion of targets with a Leader, Fort or Citadel. The actual Rampage executor already uses the full available capacity and checks legality.

source_refs.description: Roman R1 responds to immediate enemy Battle or Rampage that can force Legion/Caesar Loss.
Rampage requires Hidden Belgic Warbands and either Ambiorix within one Region or a local Successor.
The target cannot have a Leader, Citadel or Fort. One victim is affected per selected Hidden Warband, with no two-victim cap.

code_refs.description: Stale comment caps victims at two, and the min(2, hidden) condition omits legality checks.
Actual capacity is the smaller of the Hidden Warband count and the target mobile-piece count.

findings.controls: Five cases differ only in Hidden Warband count, Roman Auxilia count, adjacent Ambiorix or a local Fort. Roman Control is retained throughout; no enemy Ally, Leader or Control independently triggers R1. Ordinary enemy Battle Losses are no greater than the Auxilia count in every case. No adjacent Roman-controlled refuge exists in the legal casualty witnesses.
findings.prior_relation: The original CMD-RAMPAGE-COUNT finding fixed actor quantity and the NPC execution cap on 4 November. This distinct Roman threat consumer still retains the old two-victim assumption. Neither that ledger nor the subsequent comparison ledgers of 21, 15, 16 and 11 findings lists Roman threat eligibility or capacity.
findings.comparator_pattern: docs/audit_set_but_never_applied_s76.md section 5: real consumer and planning consumer drift; coin-implementation-lessons.md D per-space leader scope.
findings.suggested_repair: Share source-correct Rampage Region and target legality and capacity with R1, while retaining the immediate-threat interpretation and accounting for permissible Retreats and protected Roman Leaders.

findings.title: Germans Phase Rally places multiple Allies in one Region and compounds their Warband gain
findings.expected: With two German Warbands controlling Sugambri and both its Tribes Subdued, place exactly one German Ally at Suebi (North), then one German Warband in Sugambri. The ordinary one-Ally-per-Region rule still applies to the Germans Phase.
findings.observed: Both the public Germans Phase Rally and complete public germans_phase place Allies at Suebi (North) and Sugambri in the same Rally. Sugambri then receives two Warbands. The extra Ally persists through the complete phase.
findings.cause: germans_phase_rally creates one candidate per Tribe and visits the Suebi/Germania/elsewhere lists without a Region-already-used guard. Its second phase then computes the Warband quota from the inflated Ally count.

source_refs.quote: First, Rally to place as many Germanic Allied Tribes as possible per the Rally procedure (3.3.1, 3.4.1), starting with Suebi
In each selected Region ... If it Controls the Region (1.6), place one of its Ally pieces
Place a Germanic Ally only if the Region already has Germanic Control ... Then place Germanic Warbands up to the number of Germanic Allied Tribes

findings.controls: With Sugambri Tribe already German-allied, the same routine places only Suebi (North), which is legal. Running the ordinary Rally helper's Ally and Warbands options on the original fixture produces the required single Ally and single new Warband.
findings.prior_relation: Earlier original/second/third/fourth/fifth audit ledgers contain no Germans Phase per-Region Rally quota finding. BE3-01 concerns Consuetudine Ambush eligibility and Scouted hiding; ordinary Arverni Phase Rally repairs concern a different faction and command implementation.
findings.comparator_pattern: coin-implementation-lessons.md C and D: a scheduled procedure's separate implementation must preserve the normal command's per-space limits.
findings.repair_scope: Track Regions already receiving a German Ally across all three priority lists; retain Suebi-first ordering and place Warbands after the legal Ally choices.
findings.fixture: Controlled build_initial_state position in The Great Revolt, seed1, canonical place_piece and named Ally helper only. Permanent Provincia Fort retained. Pre/post validate_state and check_structural_integrity pass, including named Tribe restrictions. No sampled-game frequency claim.
findings.limits: The primary witness proves one Germanic Region with two Subdued Tribes. Similar multi-Tribe Regions follow the same loop but are not separately counted.

findings.title: Germans Phase March moves arriving Warbands a second time
findings.expected: Form original moving groups at March start. From Ubii5 and Sugambri3 (no German Allies), the original groups are four and two; each can move only into one adjacent Region. An arrival at Sugambri cannot join Sugambri's later group.
findings.observed: Seed0 marches four Warbands Ubii to Sugambri, then six Sugambri to Nervii. Sugambri started with only three Warbands, so at least three arriving pieces moved a second time. The complete Germans Phase also reproduces: after Rally Sugambri has five original Warbands, receives six from Ubii, and then sends eleven to Nervii.
findings.cause: candidate_origins saves each original warband_count, but actual_send recomputes the full current surplus after previous groups have arrived. The movement loop consumes current physical stacks without an original-piece cohort limit.

source_refs.quote: form a group of Germanic Warbands to March out of each Region
Move into at most one Region with each group (3.3.2, 3.4.2).
Germanic Warbands within a March origin Region may form at most a single moving Group to enter one adjacent Region

findings.controls: The identical original position at seed1 routes the first group elsewhere, so later groups do not exceed their original inventories; census and structure remain clean in both versions. Both isolated public March and complete public germans_phase reproduce seed0.
findings.prior_relation: Original BE-01 Germanic Chieftains/German Allegiances/Aduatuca repairs established original cohorts for human Event-guided movement. Their reports explicitly distinguish those guided Commands from the game-run Germans Phase. FE5-02 concerns transit drop-off decisions, not this separate automatic March implementation.
findings.comparator_pattern: coin-implementation-lessons.md B and C: preserving original action participants across a separate scheduled execution path.
findings.repair_scope: Preserve the original March groups and physical visibility cohorts; use only those original pieces when executing later origins, while respecting live Control and printed destination priorities.
findings.fixture: Controlled Great Revolt build_initial_state seed0: German Warbands Ubii5, Sugambri3, Treveri1, Sequani1, permanent Provincia Fort. No piece counts directly edited. Pre/post inventories and structure pass. Complete Germans Phase variant uses the actual Rally output to establish each origin's March-start inventory.
findings.limits: The no-Rally witness independently isolates the March defect; the complete-phase witness also contains WS6-01's extra Allies, but its double-movement proof is relative to the actual post-Rally inventory and does not depend on the Rally expectation.

findings.title: Germans Phase March omits player-Control priority among newly controllable destinations
findings.expected: A four-Warband group at Ubii can add Germanic Control at empty Sugambri, empty Sequani, or Treveri with one human Roman Auxilia. It must select Treveri: within destinations that add Control, prioritize player-controlled Regions.
findings.observed: At seed0 the public Germans Phase March selects empty Sugambri instead. In a complete phase on seed1, Germans instead move seven Warbands to empty Sequani while leaving the human Roman Treveri force untouched. The add-Control tier gives player-controlled and empty Regions equal random chances.
findings.cause: add_control candidates are appended before the human-control test, which runs only in the branch for destinations where the moving group cannot gain Control. Thus the printed secondary priority never applies within the highest tier.

source_refs.quote: Select destination Regions first so that the moving groups can add Germanic Control ... then (among such Regions if possible, otherwise among others) Regions that are Controlled by player Factions

findings.controls: Changing Romans to NP removes the mandatory player preference, making the same empty-Sugambri selection legal. Giving human Romans twelve Auxilia makes Treveri unconquerable, so newly controllable empty Sugambri correctly has priority. Seed1 on the direct fixture happens to select Treveri, showing the current result depends on random selection rather than the source-required preference.
findings.prior_relation: No earlier finding addresses this game-run German destination secondary priority. NP4-01 concerns Roman March opponent-strength ranking, and WS6-02 concerns original movement participants rather than destination ranking.
findings.comparator_pattern: coin-implementation-lessons.md E: conditional branches and ordered bot/procedure priorities must match the printed specification without collapsing nested tiers.
findings.repair_scope: Implement lexicographic destination priority: adds Germanic Control, then player-controlled, then seeded random tie; preserve player/non-player distinction in both conquerable and unconquerable tiers.
findings.fixture: Controlled Great Revolt build_initial_state: Ubii5 German Warbands, Treveri1 Roman Auxilia (human), permanent Provincia Fort, other playable seats NP. Direct witness seed0, full phase seed1. All pieces placed through helpers; pre/post census/structure and named Tribe restrictions pass.
findings.limits: No claims about occurrence frequency or aggregate winner drift. Complete phase uses actual post-Rally group size and still has a uniquely required player-controlled destination.
